dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: Why is discrepancy always inevitable at this point of calculation...?

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: Before I answer your question, let me ask you one: What do you think Teyvat is like?

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: You don't have to respond, just think.

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: I have a revolutionary idea... If Teyvat was round, that would explain a lot of things.

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: Why are there currents in oceans? Why would the sun and moon alternate rising? Why would there be changes in temperature?

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: All that could be explained with the round-earth theory!

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: My theory is perfect, but the calculation of land surface doesn't bear that out...

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: Damn it, I shouldn't have ditched math classes in school! It's all Vikram's fault!

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: That's because he asked me to skip classes with him. Whenever there was a class he found boring, he would grab me and have coffee in the downtown area.

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: But that guy did surprisingly well in all the foundation courses. I suspect that he dragged me out of classes on purpose, while he studied by himself at night.

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: Ah, time passes so quickly. I didn't expect him to be a candidate for the next Grand Conservator now.

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: I hope he gets elected so I can go around telling everyone that I skipped classes with the Grand Conservator back in the day.
